system_description.narrative_title: Cascading Wars, Rising Rates, and Tech Rivalries
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system in flux where overlapping kinetic conflicts (Iran war, Houthi-Saudi exchanges, Russia–Ukraine) produce energy shocks and geopolitical risk that amplify financial stress. Central-bank tightening and a bond-market reprice interact with oil-price spikes to create stagflationary pressure, while strategic competition over semiconductors, AI and supply chains is fragmenting trade and alliance architectures. Multilateral institutions and ad‑hoc coalitions are strained as states recalibrate partnerships to secure energy, munitions and technology, producing non-linear feedbacks across security, markets and industry.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and coalitions, militaries and non-state combatants, global financial markets and central banks, energy and commodity flows, semiconductor and AI supply chains, major multinational firms, and multilateral institutions (EU, NATO, UN).
system_description.super_system: The planetary political-economic-security ecosystem: integrated global markets, interstate diplomacy and transnational risk networks.
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy markets and commodity supply chains
International financial and monetary system (rates, bonds, central banks)
High-tech industrial ecosystem (semiconductors, AI, critical minerals)

variables.name: Iran‑led regional escalation
variables.description: Iran, the United States, Saudi Arabia and allied proxies (notably the Houthis) are engaged in an expanding campaign of strikes and counterstrikes that is shifting the regional military balance and raising risks of wider confrontation.

variables.name: Russia‑Ukraine high‑intensity war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain locked in large‑scale hostilities marked by aerial and drone offensives and evolving Western arms support that are changing front‑line dynamics and logistics across the battlefield.

variables.name: U.S.‑China tech and trade competition
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting dominance in semiconductors, AI and related supply chains through investment shifts, export controls and legal measures that are realigning global tech production and market access.

variables.name: Global bond‑market and central‑bank tightening shock
variables.description: A simultaneous surge in bond yields and a synchronized tightening cycle by major central banks (Fed, BOJ, BoE and others) is repricing risk, elevating borrowing costs and altering capital flows worldwide.

variables.name: Western alliance strain and realignment
variables.description: Shifts in U.S. policy under the Trump administration, EU outreach (including closer Canada‑EU ties) and transatlantic debates over trade, defence burden‑sharing and multilateralism are reshaping NATO and broader Western partnerships.
